content.title: About
content.content: Cheese, Mexican blend (540) is a semi‑hard cheese infused with the bold flavors of chili, paprika and other spices typical of Mexican cuisine. Made from cow’s milk, it has a slightly spicy bite and a golden‑orange hue derived from natural seasonings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese is commonly used in tacos, burritos and fajitas to add a distinctive aroma.
Traditional recipes include smoked chilies, cumin and garlic, giving it a rich flavor profile.
It is especially popular in U.S. regions with strong Mexican food demand, such as Texas and California.
The cheese can be sliced thinly or grated, making it versatile for cooking.
Sodium content is usually higher than in plain cheeses because of the added spices.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Provides high‑quality milk protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Rich in calcium and phosphorus, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic cultures
items.content: Some versions are produced with live cultures that may benefit gut health.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Contains monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that can support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Lactose content may cause discomfort for those who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Added spices increase sodium levels; people with hypertension should limit portions.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergic reactions to casein can occur in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese is energy‑dense; excessive consumption may contribute to weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mexican blend cheese works well as a topping for tacos, burritos, casseroles, and as a flavorful addition to salads and soups. It can be sliced, grated, or melted into sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. For longer storage (over 2‑3 weeks) it can be frozen after portioning. Discard if mold, off‑odor, or slimy texture appears.
